# Exercise 1: Summary statistics functions

**Task:** Make functions that calculate summary statistics and apply them to a variable to show that they work.



We use miles per gallon (`mpg`) from the built-in mtcars data.

```{r}
x <- mtcars$mpg
x
```

 Write the functions
 
 
# Mean: add everything up, divide by how many values 
```{r}
my_mean <- function(x){
  total <- sum(x)
  n <- length(x)
  result <- total / n
  return(result)
}
```
 
Median: the middle value after sorting
```{r}
my_median <- function(x){
  sorted <- sort(x)
  n <- length(x)
  if (n %% 2 == 1){
    result <- sorted[(n + 1) / 2]  
  } else {
    result <- (sorted[n/2] + sorted[n/2 + 1]) / 2
  }
  return(result)
}
```
 
Range: biggest minus smallest
```{r}
my_range <- function(x){
  result <- max(x) - min(x)
  return(result)
}
```


Variance: average squared distance from the mean
```{r}
my_var <- function(x){
  m <- my_mean(x)
  result <- sum((x - m)^2) / (length(x) - 1)
  return(result)
}
```


Standard deviation: square root of the variance
```{r}

my_sd <- function(x){
  result <- sqrt(my_var(x))
  return(result)
}
```



###### Applying the functions

```{r}
my_mean(x)
my_median(x)
my_range(x)
my_var(x)
my_sd(x)
```

checking if they work they work

We compare our results with R's built-in functions. They should match.

```{r}
# Side-by-side comparison table
comparison <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c("Mean", "Median", "Range", "Variance", "SD"),
  My_Function = c(my_mean(x), my_median(x), my_range(x), my_var(x), my_sd(x)),
  Built_in = c(mean(x), median(x), max(x) - min(x), var(x), sd(x))
)
comparison

# TRUE means the values match
all.equal(my_mean(x), mean(x))
all.equal(my_sd(x), sd(x))
```



# Exercise 2: Two-sample t-test function

**Task:** Make a function to calculate a two-sample t-test, then apply it to a variable.



We compare the mpg of automatic cars (am == 0) with manual cars (am == 1).

```{r}
group1 <- mtcars$mpg[mtcars$am == 0]   # automatic
group2 <- mtcars$mpg[mtcars$am == 1]   # manual
```

Write the function

```{r}
my_t_test <- function(x, y){
  # sizes
  n1 <- length(x)
  n2 <- length(y)

  # means and variances (our own functions from Exercise 1)
  mean1 <- my_mean(x)
  mean2 <- my_mean(y)
  var1  <- my_var(x)
  var2  <- my_var(y)

  # pooled variance
  pooled_var <- ((n1 - 1) * var1 + (n2 - 1) * var2) / (n1 + n2 - 2)

  # standard error of the difference
  se <- sqrt(pooled_var * (1/n1 + 1/n2))

  # t statistic and degrees of freedom
  t_value <- (mean1 - mean2) / se
  df <- n1 + n2 - 2

  # two-sided p-value
  p_value <- 2 * pt(-abs(t_value), df)

  result <- c(Mean_1 = mean1,
              Mean_2 = mean2,
              t = t_value,
              df = df,
              p_value = p_value)
  return(result)
}
```

Apply it

```{r}
res <- my_t_test(group1, group2)
res
```

## Step 5: Show that it works

We use `var.equal = TRUE` because our function pools the variances.

```{r}
t.test(group1, group2, var.equal = TRUE)
```



Interpret the result

```{r}
if (res["p_value"] < 0.05){
  print("Significant difference between the groups")
} else {
  print("No significant difference between the groups")
}
```

Because p < 0.05, manual and automatic cars differ in mean mpg.

Welch's t-test (R's default)

```{r}
my_welch_t_test <- function(x, y){
  n1 <- length(x)
  n2 <- length(y)
  mean1 <- my_mean(x)
  mean2 <- my_mean(y)
  var1  <- my_var(x)
  var2  <- my_var(y)

  se <- sqrt(var1/n1 + var2/n2)
  t_value <- (mean1 - mean2) / se
  df <- (var1/n1 + var2/n2)^2 /
        ((var1/n1)^2/(n1 - 1) + (var2/n2)^2/(n2 - 1))
  p_value <- 2 * pt(-abs(t_value), df)

  result <- c(Mean_1 = mean1, Mean_2 = mean2,
              t = t_value, df = df, p_value = p_value)
  return(result)
}

my_welch_t_test(group1, group2)
t.test(group1, group2)   # should match
```
